xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-1966: Single authoritative pipeline-membership resolver — one function for "what's in the pipeline" (collapse the 5 divergent views)

plan.title: Single authoritative pipeline-membership resolver — one function for "what's in the pipeline" (collapse the 5 divergent views)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Pipeline membership ("what's in the pipeline") is computed in 6 independent places from different signal subsets — resource-discovery (L5 liveness + tracker state), frontend pipeline-state (labels + review_status DB), pan pending (review_status rows only), enumerate-in-flight (open issue ∩ workspace dir), flywheel (LLM judgment + workspace-dir existence), and the pipeline-status skill (tracker-state filter). They drift, producing zombie PRs, post-merge limbo, and ghost worktrees that no surface owns. The authoritative classifier resolvePipelineMembership() already exists (src/lib/pipeline-membership.ts, PAN-1980) with 8/8 unit tests, but NOTHING in production imports it — the only importer is its own test.
narratives.Proposal: Extend the shipped resolver with two additive pieces (a hasVbriefSpec lens so planned issues are members per the 2026-07-16 operator comment, and a labelDrift annotation for FR-4). Build one batch lens-signal gatherer over durable sources only (GitHub issues+labels, open/merged PR lists, feature/* branches + squash-aware merge checks, specs on overdeck-state). Expose the read door as a cached server service + GET /api/pipeline/membership. Rewire all 6 sites to delegate: in-process TS consumers import the lib; out-of-process consumers (pipeline-status skill, flywheel orchestrator prompt) hit the endpoint. Land a no-loss audit test enumerating every legacy consumer, and an import-boundary lint guard so no site can regrow independent membership math. L5 (DB/state.json/tmux) becomes annotation-only everywhere.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No orphan_branch bucket: closed issue + leftover branch stays clean_terminal per shipped PAN-1980 §2d (only an open PR makes a closed issue a zombie_pr)
- No changes to phase-within-pipeline lane semantics (getPipelineIssuePhase lanes stay; only the membership gate moves to the resolver)
- No removal of the review_status table or any L5 surface — they remain phase/liveness annotations
- No PAN-1965 view/UI work (lens matrix rendering is the consumer issue)
- No new pan CLI verb (pan pending is rewired; no pan pipeline command)
- No DoR/DoD redesign (the interim Ready-lane behavior is preserved, not extended)
- No destructive cutover acceptance test (never 'rm ~/.overdeck and observe' — mechanical import-graph assertion instead)

autoDecisions.summary: Planned membership = new durable lens hasVbriefSpec (spec present on overdeck-state via findSpecByIssue); the GitHub 'planned' label is a hint only.
autoDecisions.rationale: Operator comment 2026-07-16 requires planned issues in the pipeline; the label is applied on a swallowed-failure path (planning-promotion.ts:646) and actively stripped by label-reconciler/close-issue, so spec presence is the only reliable durable signal.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the shipped resolver's bucket set (no orphan_branch bucket) and classification semantics; scope this issue to extensions + wiring.
autoDecisions.rationale: The 2026-06-19 issue comment declares the resolver built and shipped with the remaining work being wiring; PAN-1980 §2d deliberately decided closed ⇒ terminal except open PR.

autoDecisions.summary: FR-4 label drift ships as an additive labelDrift annotation field on PipelineMembership, not as new buckets.
autoDecisions.rationale: Drift direction is orthogonal to membership; annotation preserves the 5-bucket contract PAN-1965 will render.

autoDecisions.summary: Read door = GET /api/pipeline/membership for out-of-process consumers; pan pending calls the shared lib directly.
autoDecisions.rationale: The CLI must work when the dashboard is down; both transports execute the same single gather+resolve module, so membership math still exists exactly once (FR-5).

autoDecisions.summary: One vBRIEF rather than sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: All wiring items share one foundation (the gatherer) and one exit gate (no-loss audit + lint guard); sibling issues would fragment the audit FR-5 requires.

autoDecisions.summary: hasMergedPr gathered from one batched merged-PR listing per project (--limit 500), with isBranchMerged (close-out.ts:97) as the squash-aware per-branch fallback.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids N+1 gh API calls; merges old enough to fall off the limit pair with closed issues, which are clean_terminal regardless.

items.title: Extend resolver: hasVbriefSpec lens makes planned issues pipeline members

expected_outputs: all pipeline-membership tests pass including new planned-lens cases

narrative.Action: Add `hasVbriefSpec: boolean` to IssueLensSignals in src/lib/pipeline-membership.ts (doc comment: durable — vBRIEF spec exists on the overdeck-state git branch; gather via findSpecByIssue, never from the DB). In resolvePipelineMembership, change the final open-issue branch: when the issue is open with no PR (open or merged) and no live/convention branch, return `planned_backlog` (inPipeline: true) if `hasVbriefSpec` is true, with reason 'open issue with a vBRIEF spec but no branch/PR — planned work whose plan encodes code paths that age; needs starting or re-planning'; otherwise keep the existing clean_terminal 'backlog, never started' result. Closed issues are unaffected (spec never overrides closed ⇒ terminal). Update the test file's sig() helper with a `hasVbriefSpec: false` default and add the new cases. Update the module header comment to list the new lens (call it L6-spec).

items.title: Given an open issue with hasVbriefSpec true and all other lenses false, resolvePipelineMembership returns bucket planned_backlog with inPipeline true
Given a closed issue with hasVbriefSpec true and no open PR, the resolver returns clean_terminal (a spec never overrides closed ⇒ terminal)
The pipeline-membership test suite passes with all 8 pre-existing PAN-1980 cases unchanged, hasVbriefSpec defaulting to false in the sig() helper
Add labelDrift annotation to PipelineMembership (FR-4, both directions)

narrative.Action: Add `labelDrift: 'stale_present' | 'stale_absent' | null` to PipelineMembership in src/lib/pipeline-membership.ts, computed inside resolvePipelineMembership: 'stale_present' when the result bucket is clean_terminal (or the issue is closed) but phaseLabel is non-null; 'stale_absent' when hasOpenPr is true but phaseLabel is null; otherwise null. Do not change any bucket outcomes — this is a pure annotation. The phaseLabel values are whatever the gatherer maps from the canonical pipeline label set (src/lib/cloister/label-reconciler.ts:9 STALE_PIPELINE_LABELS is the reference list — quote it in a comment). Add test cases.

items.title: Given a closed issue with phaseLabel 'in-progress' and no open PR, the result carries labelDrift 'stale_present' and bucket clean_terminal
Given an open issue with an open PR and phaseLabel null, the result carries labelDrift 'stale_absent' and bucket in_flight
Given an open in_flight issue with phaseLabel 'in-review', labelDrift is null and no bucket changes versus the pre-change classification
Batch lens-signal gatherer from durable sources (git + GitHub + specs)

expected_outputs: gatherer unit tests pass with mocked gh/git

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/pipeline-membership-gather.ts exporting `gatherProjectLensSignals(project): Promise<IssueLensSignals[]>`. Candidate universe = dedup-by-issue-id union of: (a) open GitHub issues with labels (listOpenIssuesWithLabelsPromise, src/lib/github-app.ts:601); (b) issue ids parsed from open-PR head branches `feature/<id>` (pattern: loadOpenPullRequests, src/dashboard/server/services/resource-discovery.ts:345 — gh pr list --state open --json number,state,headRefName); (c) local+remote feature/* convention branches (pattern: loadProjectBranches, resource-discovery.ts:383); (d) issues with a vBRIEF spec (findSpecByIssue, src/lib/pan-dir/specs.ts:224, or its sync variant). Lens fills: issueOpen from (a) membership or getIssueStatePromise (github-app.ts:592) for candidates not in the open set; hasOpenPr from (b); hasMergedPr from ONE batched `gh pr list --state merged --json headRefName,mergedAt --limit 500` (never per-issue calls); hasConventionBranch from (c); branchUnmerged via `git for-each-ref --no-merged=main` batch (pattern: loadBranchesAheadOfMain, resource-discovery.ts:422) — the resolver's L1-merged pairing already corrects the squash blind spot (FR-3); phaseLabel = first label in the canonical set from label-reconciler.ts:9; hasVbriefSpec from (d). HARD CONSTRAINTS: async exec only (execAsync/spawn — no execSync, this is server-reachable, PAN-70); the module must import NOTHING from the SQLite DB layer, review-status, agent state, or tmux modules (NFR-1 — membership must be computable with an empty overdeck.db). Unit tests mock the gh/git executor and assert candidate union, lens values, batching (call counts), and the squash case end-to-end through resolvePipelineMembership.

items.title: Given mocked sources containing an open issue, an open-PR-only branch, a branch-only issue, and a spec-only issue, gatherProjectLensSignals returns one deduplicated IssueLensSignals per issue with all six lenses filled
Given any candidate count, the gatherer emits exactly one merged-PR listing call (test asserts executor call counts — no per-issue gh calls)
A squash-merged branch (merged PR exists, lineage says unmerged) produces signals that resolve to post_merge_limbo, not planned_backlog, when passed through resolvePipelineMembership
A test asserts the module's import graph contains no DB/review-status/agent-state/tmux modules, so gathering succeeds against a fresh empty overdeck.db by construction
The module contains no execSync/spawnSync calls (async exec only), verified by the existing dashboard-server lint rules passing with the new file in scope
Pipeline-membership read door: cached service + GET /api/pipeline/membership

expected_outputs: typecheck and lint complete without errors

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/server/services/pipeline-membership.ts: a service that runs gatherProjectLensSignals + resolvePipelineMembership per project behind a short TTL cache (~30s, matching resource-discovery's cache idiom) so bursty consumers don't stampede gh. Add route GET /api/pipeline/membership?project=<key> returning the array of PipelineMembership objects (issueId, inPipeline, bucket, reasons, lenses, labelDrift). Register in the existing route composition (src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts or a new small route module wired in server.ts — follow the 12-route-module structure). This endpoint is the pipeline domain's read door for out-of-process consumers (pipeline-status skill, flywheel orchestrator). No DB reads in the service.

items.title: GET /api/pipeline/membership returns a JSON array where each element carries issueId, inPipeline, bucket, reasons, lenses, and labelDrift for the requested project
Given two calls within the TTL, the endpoint returns cached results and the gatherer runs exactly once (fake-timer test, no real sleeps)
The route responds through the registered Effect route composition (server route table includes it; a request against the test harness returns 200)

Rewire resource-discovery membership through the resolver; L5 becomes annotation-only

expected_outputs: resource-discovery tests pass with resolver-gated membership

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/server/services/resource-discovery.ts, replace the membership predicate chain in computeResourceAllocatedIssues (lines ~764-806, helpers isLiveResource/isActiveTrackerState/isTerminalTrackerState/hasOpenPr at ~261-284) with resolvePipelineMembership over signals from gatherProjectLensSignals (the service already loads most raw inputs — reuse its loaders where they match, but the membership decision must come from the resolver only). tmux/docker/remote-agent/conversation/readyForMerge signals become annotations on the emitted issue (which resources exist), never membership. Per decision D7: an issue with live resources whose verdict is clean_terminal is still emitted, flagged with an orphan-resource drift marker (additive field, e.g. resourceDrift: true) so the Command Deck tree loses nothing silently. Add each issue's bucket to toPublicResourceIssue output (additive). Keep the /api/issues/resource-allocated route shape backward-compatible (only additions).

items.title: Given an issue whose only signals are an in_progress tracker state with no durable lenses, computeResourceAllocatedIssues returns no membership for it — resolvePipelineMembership alone decides

narrative.Action: Add an optional pipelineMembership field ({ inPipeline: boolean; bucket: PipelineBucket; labelDrift: string | null }) to the issue DTO in packages/contracts (rebuild contracts after editing — workspace rule). Populate it server-side where issues are served to the frontend (the issues route / enrichment that feeds the store), sourced from the cached membership service. In src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/pipeline-state.ts, make the MEMBERSHIP decision (isPipelineReady at lines 116-125 and any todo-hiding gates) read the server-computed field when present, falling back to current behavior when absent (older cached DTOs). Do NOT change getPipelineIssuePhase lane assignment for in-pipeline issues — phase-within-pipeline stays as-is. Surface bucket so PAN-1965 can render it later (no UI work here beyond the gate).

narrative.Action: In src/cli/commands/pending.ts, derive the issue universe from gatherProjectLensSignals + resolvePipelineMembership (direct lib call — the CLI must work with the dashboard down). No-loss audit test: every legacy view's consumers accounted for, drift table pinned

expected_outputs: audit test passes, enumerating all six sites

narrative.Action: Create tests/unit/lib/pipeline-membership-audit.test.ts implementing the refactor rule's no-loss audit gate. Part 1 — delegation: for each of the six sites (resource-discovery.ts, frontend pipeline-state.ts, cli/commands/pending.ts, reconstruct/enumerate-in-flight.ts, cloister/flywheel.ts, skills/pipeline-status/SKILL.md), read the file content and assert it references the resolver path (imports resolvePipelineMembership / gatherProjectLensSignals, reads the DTO pipelineMembership field, or names /api/pipeline/membership) AND no longer contains its named legacy predicate (e.g. isActiveTrackerState gating membership, the openIssueIds∩FEATURE_DIR_RE gate, the in_progress/in_review tracker filter). Part 2 — behavior: a table-driven run of resolvePipelineMembership pinning the issue's acceptance drift cases (closed+openPR→zombie_pr; open+mergedPR→post_merge_limbo; open+spec-only→planned_backlog; squash-merged branch→post_merge_limbo not planned_backlog; closed+branch-only→clean_terminal). This test is the gate that blocks silent replacement — if a future change removes a site's delegation, it goes red.

items.title: The audit test fails when any of the six sites drops its resolver delegation (verified by the assertions reading each site's source and matching resolver usage)
The audit test fails when a named legacy membership predicate reappears in a site (negative pattern assertions per site)
The drift-case table passes: zombie_pr, post_merge_limbo, planned_backlog (spec-only), squash-merge, and closed-branch cases classify exactly as the issue's acceptance criteria state
Import-boundary lint guard: membership math only in the resolver module

expected_outputs: guard exits 0 on the current tree
npm run lint invokes the guard and passes

narrative.Action: Create scripts/lint-pipeline-membership.sh modeled on scripts/lint-overdeck-boundaries.sh (grep-based boundary gate with counted violations and clear per-violation messages). It fails when: (1) any of the six consumer sites no longer imports/references the resolver path; (2) a consumer site matches a banned legacy-membership pattern (maintain the pattern list in the script with a comment per site); (3) src/lib/pipeline-membership-gather.ts or src/lib/pipeline-membership.ts imports DB/review-status/agent-state/tmux modules (NFR-1 boundary). Include a self-test mode (--self-test) that runs the checks against embedded fixture snippets and asserts a seeded violation is caught, so the guard's own detection is verifiable without mutating the tree. Wire it into npm run lint in package.json alongside the existing lint-*.sh scripts.

items.title: scripts/lint-pipeline-membership.sh exits 0 on the current tree and npm run lint invokes it
The guard's --self-test mode exits non-zero for a seeded violation fixture (a consumer computing membership without the resolver) and reports which pattern matched
The guard rejects a DB/agent-state/tmux import inside pipeline-membership-gather.ts (seeded self-test fixture demonstrates the NFR-1 boundary)

Add a short 'Pipeline membership — the canonical resolver' section to CLAUDE.md pointing at the doc and the module, mirroring the existing 'Decisions' section's style.
